{"command":"change context","version":"0.1.0","status":"pass","exit_code":0,"data":{"schema_version":"agent-context/v1","entry_id":"ev_01M61RB2S36P4YXNEBAC532HCF","session_id":"01a181a7-5bb2-7f30-8811-5107e3b5ac0e","change_id":"2026-10-27-harness-knowledge-context","authority_digest":"23bb205c1697bf7c61ff661a9a93a459c50ded305d24b7d8b9acb06522bdc649","delivery_id":"context-ev_01M61RB2S36P4YXNEBAC532HCF-23bb205c1697bf7c61ff661a9a93a459c50ded305d24b7d8b9acb06522bdc649","context_digest":"12c282f085f6cc423adc09d030d8cc0d38fde1d2fa3c5b2aec5b292f6ad2c64f","manifest_id":"2a9fae963511783a2438466702bfd730ec9e174d5710fca357a862ece9b5cd1b","page":6,"total_pages":8,"content":"ied_at\":\"2026-06-26T09:45:28.846809Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-dangling-check.md\",\"source_digest\":\"848ee5d7e381146b7ddc674f76062673cd33e5a49bb78fa96a85607c903c54d4\",\"version\":\"sha256:d1aa4710844e840396baf69320b33fa30565d79879eb8c0c0ab03d6a7f2273b2\"},{\"body\":\"Decisions are one-file-per-record under docs/decisions/, four-state lifecycle.\\n\\n```review\\nDecisions are stored one-file-per-record at docs/decisions/<id>.md with a four-state\\nlifecycle (proposed -> ratified -> superseded / retired). The loader in decisions.py\\nenforces this shape; there is no multi-record file and no fifth state. On any change\\nto decisions.py, confirm the one-file-per-record model and the four-state lifecycle\\nare preserved. Still holds -> `decision reconcile d-decision-records`; broken ->\\n`decision betray d-decision-records` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-decision-records\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-06-26T09:45:29.090702Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-decision-records.md\",\"source_digest\":\"ad6d49edd78cb7a3894b16a14b4fdb9e59a5cddaec6a9031ec70c0a09da5cd0b\",\"version\":\"sha256:b2ee29066411206363cb90de2251e44e17d4f53bca0c4d4018fc9dd538f4badd\"},{\"body\":\"Events are append-only; the log is the source of truth, state is derived.\\n\\n```review\\nThe Event dataclass is frozen and events.jsonl is append-only: events are appended\\nand never edited, reordered, or truncated in place; the log stays the single source\\nof truth and all state is a derived fold over it (see d-state-pure-fold), never\\npersisted as the authority. On any change to the Event model or the event writer,\\nconfirm no path mutates/truncates an existing event and that state remains\\nlog-derived. Still holds -> `decision reconcile d-events-append-only`; broken ->\\n`decision betray d-events-append-only` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-events-append-only\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-06-26T09:45:08.963090Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-events-append-only.md\",\"source_digest\":\"bd8e91bb3e24ad71820b5c643bda2872e53d1595cb638450580e1ba02ea046a9\",\"version\":\"sha256:8db7275f6ea859c6e8ada8b4e77ec8a954024d45bffcc6a822ede1d62f69254b\"},{\"body\":\"State transitions come only from the fixed declared matrix; no ad-hoc transition.\\n\\n```review\\nEvery state transition is looked up in the fixed declared `_TRANSITIONS` matrix (via\\ncompute_target_state); no module computes or assigns a change's state through an\\nad-hoc transition outside this table. On any change to transitions.py, confirm the\\nmatrix remains the sole source of transitions and no hardcoded/ad-hoc state change\\nwas introduced elsewhere. Still holds -> `decision reconcile d-fixed-transition-matrix`;\\nbroken -> `decision betray d-fixed-transition-matrix` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-fixed-transition-matrix\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-06-26T09:45:27.695262Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-fixed-transition-matrix.md\",\"source_digest\":\"a1b4aed21ad4c7f7b641dfdd9c3857f83765bc4d023dd2bc0bd3f8c1ef0e2947\",\"version\":\"sha256:bd22ae2dcac7f0630529e2d42457b809858d2ca19e33a4bf870b1bc76b1ba52b\"},{\"body\":\"The pre-tool-use gate governs files that will enter git as product; its allowances are hard-coded path whitelists, never derived from gitignore status.\\n\\nThe gate's job is to stop unreviewed *product* from being written before its plan is\\napproved. It is not to stop the change from thinking. Blocking a file no reviewer will\\never see buys no safety �� it only makes the harness something to route around, and this\\nproject has already watched that happen: with no legal way to revise a rejected plan,\\n\\\"write it through the shell\\\" became documented procedure in its own pothole list.\\n\\nHence the narrowings in `gates.decisions`: the change's plan document (`INTENT_DECLARED`,\\n`PLAN_PATH_ALLOW_STATES`), its recorded plan artifacts (`PLAN_REJECTED`,\\n`PLAN_ARTIFACT_ALLOW_STATES`), and its scratch area (`SCRATCH_ROOT`, every state).\\n\\n**Why allowances are never derived from gitignore status.** \\\"Ignored by git, therefore\\nharmless\\\" is the obvious shortcut and it is fatal. These are all gitignored:\\n\\n| path | what it is |\\n|---|---|\\n| `.harness/gate-disabled` | the gate's own kill switch |\\n| `.claude/settings.local.json` | the hook registration that installs the gate |\\n| `.codex/hooks.json` | the same, for Codex |\\n| `.harness/state.yaml` | the state the gate reads to decide |\\n\\nUnder a gitignore-derived rule, an agent blocked from editing source could simply write\\n`.harness/gate-disabled` and the gate would be gone. Allowances must therefore be\\nhard-coded path whitelists, compared **after** `canonical_relpath` has resolved `..` and\\nsymlinks, so that a traversal out of an allowed prefix lands on its real target and\\nblocks.\\n\\n```review\\nConfirm that every allowance in `gates.decisions` is a literal, hard-coded path or\\npattern shape, and that none is computed from gitignore status, `git check-ignore`,\\n`.gitignore` contents, or any other \\\"is this tracked?\\\" test. Confirm the gate compares\\nagainst the CANONICALIZED path (post-`canonical_relpath`), so `..` and symlink escapes\\nout of an allowed prefix resolve elsewhere and block. Confirm that\\n`.harness/gate-disabled`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.codex/hooks.json` and\\n`.harness/state.yaml` are reachable by NO allowance in any lifecycle state.\\n\\nDeliberately NOT armed with an executable check: a `counterexample` block can only ADD a\\nfile, and no added file can make the gate allow a path the whitelists do not name �� so\\nany check written here would pass its bite-test for the wrong reason, i.e. be hollow.\\nRe-review by reading the four literals whenever the gate paths change.\\n\\nStill holds -> `decision reconcile d-gate-governs-git-product`; broken ->\\n`decision betray d-gate-governs-git-product` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-gate-governs-git-product\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-07-29T13:14:27.000496Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-gate-governs-git-product.md\",\"source_digest\":\"160d7619705b42f411ea81b886c0b589fb233a075a33f0f528a9a298fbde7420\",\"version\":\"sha256:5614ab4fe81201905d53b409478e0e56c63af05ff01b2d5c7b0b3a0ca8f7692b\"},{\"body\":\"core/ is the base layer: it must not import the upper layers cli/gates/sensors/engineering.\\n\\n`keepsail.core` is the pure foundation the upper layers build on. It must not\\ndepend (directly OR transitively) on the upper layers `keepsail.cli`,\\n`keepsail.gates`, `keepsail.sensors`, or `keepsail.engineering`, so the\\ncore can be imported (e.g. by the daemon) without dragging in the\\nCLI/gate/sensor/engineering stack. The faithful mechanical form\\nof this invariant is an import-graph contract, not a text grep: `grep` sees only direct\\ntextual imports and is blind to the transitive and function-local edges that actually\\nbreak layering. The rung-1 check is the import-linter `core-is-base` contract in\\n`.importlinter`.\\n\\n(`sensors` is now covered too. Two transitive `core -> sensors` edges both flowed through\\n`adapters -> sensors` (a `WorkspaceContext` re-export): `core.review_bundle -> adapters`\\nand `core.sync_check -> engineering -> adapters`. import-linter caught both where grep\\ndeclared the code clean. They were severed by moving `WorkspaceContext` into\\n`core.workspace` (so `adapters` no longer imports `sensors`) and by injecting the\\nspec/plan-path resolver into `core.review_bundle` instead of importing `adapters` there.)\\n\\n(`engineering` is now covered too (F9). Besides the transitive path above, there was a\\n*direct* `core -> engineering` edge the forbidden set had never listed: `core.sync_check`\\nimported `engineering.agents_md_render` and `engineering.gitignore_injector`. `sync_check`\\nis sync-orchestration logic that depends on nothing in `core`, so it was relocated to\\n`engineering.sync_check` (it no longer lives in `core` �� do not grep for a `core.sync_check`\\nedge), and `engineering` was added to the forbidden list. The contract now covers all four\\nupper layers cli/gates/sensors/engineering.)\\n\\n```check\\nPYTHONPATH=src lint-imports --config .importlinter --contract core-is-base --no-cache\\n```\\n\\n```counterexample path=src/keepsail/core/_ce_core_is_base.py\\nfrom keepsail.cli import plan  # forbidden: core importing an orchestration layer\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-keepsail-core-is-base\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-10-23T14:02:31.159634Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-keepsail-core-is-base.md\",\"source_digest\":\"b85f0f96656c3eb47da70181c763bca24b41d0357b13e7d3d755a6d222c029c5\",\"version\":\"sha256:3288f9d22784cfc5b5f40b4ff5e79c11146c8aee921970fd50267f965fc200b9\"},{\"body\":\"GitHub access goes through the gh CLI, never raw REST.\\n\\n`gh api /repos/...` (REST *through* gh, relative paths, never the host) is allowed.\\n\\\"Raw REST\\\" = bypassing gh to hit the API host directly. The faithful mechanical\\nsignature of that bypass is naming the host `api.github.com` in source.\\n\\n```check\\n! grep -rn 'api\\\\.github\\\\.com' src/\\n```\\n\\n```counterexample path=src/keepsail/_ce_raw_rest.py\\nimport requests\\nrequests.get(\\\"https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo\\\")\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-keepsail-gh-cli-not-rest\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-10-23T14:02:33.540862Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-keepsail-gh-cli-not-rest.md\",\"source_digest\":\"9a8d55fd1c5bb50dd8e75a2a45904d263233a8dc7baabde7778d6ebdb72b9227\",\"version\":\"sha256:81a1099345427bec038644c8c91efda883790c1b421ea30e88f00b545ee710f3\"},{\"body\":\"Identity resolution order is fixed: --as > env > git config > \\\"cli\\\".\\n\\n```review\\n`resolve_identity` resolves in the fixed precedence override(--as) > env\\nKEEPSAIL_ACTOR > git config user.email > \\\"cli\\\"; first non-empty value (after\\nstrip) wins and the result is always non-empty. On any change to identity.py, confirm\\nthis order is unchanged and no source is added or reordered. Still holds -> `decision\\nreconcile d-keepsail-identity-resolution-order`; broken -> `decision betray\\nd-keepsail-identity-resolution-order` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-keepsail-identity-resolution-order\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-10-23T14:02:35.932361Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-keepsail-identity-resolution-order.md\",\"source_digest\":\"2e7bf986e1ac0e28deea39c7d35f7dc86e9536b6cd58580db68ff8c002c4bf67\",\"version\":\"sha256:0635403d3ec9b995aace7485eed68bec0d3726632d578629a16239bf3faca765\"},{\"body\":\"The merge gate verifies committed evidence with pure git �� no network, no runtime trust.\\n\\nThe merge gate is `cli/attest.py` (subprocess only for `git diff`) + `engineering/attestation.py`\\n(pure). Both must stay free of network clients. The check scans exactly those two files ��\\n`gates/` is the PreToolUse policy, not the merge gate, and stays out of scope.\\n\\n```check\\n! grep -rnE 'import +(urllib|requests|httpx|socket)|(urllib|requests|httpx|socket)\\\\.[a-zA-Z_]|api\\\\.github\\\\.com' src/keepsail/cli/attest.py src/keepsail/engineering/attestation.py\\n```\\n\\n```counterexample path=src/keepsail/cli/attest.py\\nimport urllib.request  # raw network smuggled into the merge gate\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-keepsail-merge-gate-pure-git\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-10-23T14:02:35.654411Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-keepsail-merge-gate-pure-git.md\",\"source_digest\":\"fb8bd236576380a966f2e2d43a8c28420662805f07bea99e35bc200c9d0b7682\",\"version\":\"sha256:004673096ea486ad401cee69469337b8be2973f4539cb55ac6ede9dc13371e99\"},{\"body\":\"Negative knowledge is recorded as a proposed decision record; Keepsail grows no parallel pitfall corpus.\\n\\n\\\"Don't do this / here be dragons / doing X also requires Y\\\" is recorded with\\n`decision new`, which creates a `status: proposed` record. That state is the vessel:\\nfiling one is free �� it is absent from the `ratified` set comprehension in\\n`core/decision_check.py` that drives every verdict, and it stays out of the tier\\ntally �� and unlike a note it has an exit: `ratify` once the rule can be stated,\\n`retire` once it stops being true. There is no parallel pitfall directory, no pitfall\\nrecord type, and no hand-maintained maturity labels or usage counters.\\n\\n**Filing is free; anchoring is not.** `dangling_up` is computed against the ratified set,\\nso a `@decision:` sentinel naming a proposed id is a dangling-up reference and a hard CI\\nfailure. Do not anchor a record until it is ratified. The unqualified form of the claim\\nabove �� \\\"a proposed record cannot fail CI\\\" �� is false, and stating it that way sends an\\nagent that files a trap and then anchors it at the site it describes, which is standing\\npractice here, into a failure the guidance called impossible.\\n\\nThe field evidence is why: standalone lessons-learned repositories have a documented\\nfailure record (NASA LLIS, OIG IG-12-012), while every surviving form imposes an entry\\ncondition �� an executable detector (Clippy), a subject stable enough not to move\\n(PostgreSQL's \\\"Don't Do This\\\"), or a named replacement (AntiPatterns). A decision\\nrecord can carry all three and adds two they lack: a lifecycle that retires it, and\\nanchors that mark it suspect when the code it describes changes.\\n\\n**Ceilings, recorded deliberately.**\\n\\n(a) *The mechanism ceiling.* This record cannot be armed with a check, and that is a\\nproperty of the tooling rather than a shortfall here. A `counterexample` can only\\n*add* a file, so a check can only ever assert \\\"no file contains or creates X\\\". The\\ninvariant that actually matters �� that a `proposed` record does not gate �� is\\nbehavioural, cannot be bite-tested by adding a file, and an un-bite-tested check is\\nexactly what `ratify` refuses. Hence tier-2, whose anchor catches the failure a check\\ncould not.\\n\\n(b) *`core/decisions.py` is deliberately un-anchored.* It holds the four-state\\nlifecycle and the `decision_tier` ladder, but it is already anchored by\\n`d-decision-records`, whose subject *is* that shape. A second anchor on the same file\\nwould spend reconcile budget without raising a signal the first one does not.\\n\\n(c) *`cli/decision.py` is deliberately un-anchored.* Its `ratify` accepts `proposed`\\n(the exit path out of proposed), which is a genuine precondition, but the file churns\\nfor unrelated reasons and anchoring it would spend the reconcile budget on noise.\\n\\n```review\\nNegative knowledge is recorded as a proposed decision record; there is no parallel\\npitfall directory, no pitfall record type, no hand-maintained usage metadata. The\\nload-bearing precondition is that filing one is free: the `ratified` set comprehension in\\n`core/decision_check.py` excludes it, and that set is what drives dangling-down,\\nthe effective-ratified set, and the tier-2 suspect and unreconciled loops.\\n\\nOn any change to `core/decision_check.py`, confirm a proposed record is still absent from\\nthat set and therefore still free to file. If it is not, this decision has become advice\\nthat breaks CI, which is worse than no advice. Confirm too that the anchor sentinel still\\nsits on that set comprehension and not on the body-hash integrity filter below it �� the\\nlatter is redundant for a proposed record, so a sentinel there would point a re-reviewer\\nat a line carrying no invariant.\\n\\nNote what this criterion does *not* claim: a proposed record can still fail CI if someone\\nanchors it, because dangling-up is computed against the ratified set. Filing is free;\\nanchoring is not.\\n\\nStill holds -> `decision reconcile d-keepsail-pitfall-is-proposed-decision`; broken ->\\n`decision betray d-keepsail-pitfall-is-proposed-decision` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-keepsail-pitfall-is-proposed-decision\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-10-23T14:02:36.208295Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-keepsail-pitfall-is-proposed-decision.md\",\"source_digest\":\"a715e434248f82b20b5c91caea0fa0a51fe2b51e01fc1ef864fb20b18b23f9ed\",\"version\":\"sha256:53fd2da031aba215d2b8a4a4a3a17e279506dedbda5ef7f7c8f78e03ce3646db\"},{\"body\":\"Gate policy lives in one module (gates.decisions); the in-process gate reads it, neither invents nor forks policy.\\n\\n```review\\nThe gate decision policy lives in one module (`gates.decisions`), now in FOUR\\nliterals: the per-state `PRE_TOOL_USE_DECISIONS` matrix, `PLAN_ARTIFACT_ALLOW_STATES`\\n(the PLAN_REJECTED plan-artifact narrowing �� HG-PLAN-AUTHORING), `PLAN_PATH_ALLOW_STATES`\\n(the INTENT_DECLARED plan-document narrowing), and `SCRATCH_ROOT` (the per-change\\nscratch prefix, allowed in every state). The in-process gate (`PreToolUseGate`, shared\\nby the `keepsail-hook` decision path and the `gate check` CLI) reads these\\ndeclarations �� it does not invent, hardcode, or fork its own per-state or per-path\\nallow/block policy, and no future gate may fork them.\\n\\nEvery narrowing only ever turns a `block` into a *specific* allow; none widens to\\nsource:\\n- plan-artifact: a marked `.md` recorded by the reviewed `plan ready` submission;\\n- plan-path: a path matching an owner-configured pattern from the tracked\\n  `.harness/plan-paths.yaml`, where each pattern must contain `{slug}` (binding the\\n  allowance to the active change) and the RESOLVED path must end in `.md`;\\n- scratch: the `SCRATCH_ROOT/<change_id>/` prefix only �� gitignored, never reviewed,\\n  never merged.\\n\\nTwo invariants a reviewer must re-confirm on any gate change: (a) the allow-state sets\\nstay disjoint, so branch ordering cannot change a verdict �� there is a unit test in\\ntests/unit/gates asserting exactly this; (b) allowances are hard-coded path whitelists\\nand are NEVER derived from gitignore status �� see the d-gate-governs-git-product record.\\n\\nConfirm the reader still defers to this single SSOT module. Still holds ->\\n`decision reconcile d-keepsail-single-gate-policy`; broken -> `decision betray\\nd-keepsail-single-gate-policy` with a justification.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-keepsail-single-gate-policy\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-10-23T14:02:36.491824Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-keepsail-single-gate-policy.md\",\"source_digest\":\"426432ed035bb03a950a644289f4945801b7376f976faadfc4f2497ff771e5ce\",\"version\":\"sha256:d1c0a806764e84409b7e35ca60d5f70ef52d7dc8fb1a3f4c7f23a809df5080cc\"},{\"body\":\"State is a pure left-fold over the event log; never mutated in place.\\n\\n```review\\nreducer.derive_state is a pure left-fold over the event log: it constructs and\\nreturns a fresh state and never mutates its inputs or any module-level global in\\nplace (logging is permitted; referential transparency is about the returned value).\\nOn any change to reducer.py, re-review the anchored fold: confirm no in-place\\nmutation of the accumulator or inputs was introduced and that it stays referentially\\ntransparent (same events -> same state). If it still holds, `decision reconcile\\nd-state-pure-fold`. If purity was broken (in-place mutation or non-determinism\\nintroduced), do NOT reconcile -- `decision betray d-state-pure-fold` with a\\njustification instead.\\n```\",\"id\":\"d-state-pure-fold\",\"ratified_at\":\"2026-06-22T19:25:38.517675Z\",\"ratified_by\":\"dawinialo@163.com\",\"source\":\"docs/decisions/d-state-pure-fold.md\",\"source_digest\":\"9ba7a596979e8bdfadd37c8703708a5512b8a5c889fcb242354bd437ae1d0b23\",\"version\":\"sha256:8a106295b2f00df8c9f657c22e02af8cf6b37cee29ee005e772647d62be48ed0\"}],\"delivery_id\":\"context-ev_01M61RB2S36P4YXNEBAC532HCF-23bb205c1697bf7c61ff661a9a93a459c50ded305d24b7d8b9acb06522bdc649\",\"entry\":{\"change_id\":\"2026-10-27-harness-knowledge-context\",\"cli\":\"E:/Work/keepsail/.venv/Scripts/keepsail.EXE\",\"entry_id\":\"ev_01M61RB2S36P4YXNEBAC532HCF\",\"harness\":\"codex\",\"return_transport\":\"powershell-exit/v1\",\"root\":\"E:/Work/keepsail\",\"session_id\":\"01a181a7-5bb2-7f30-8811-5107e3b5ac0e\",\"source\":\"resume\"},\"identity\":{\"change_id\":\"2026-10-27-harness-knowledge-context\",\"current_state\":\"IMPLEMENTATION_IN_PROGRESS\",\"head\":\"4985ab","content_digest":"381da59f2acea6460a8a00f211a551cbd24be7a55e2412659c7bdebbaae4a041","utf8_bytes":19803,"token_estimate":6601,"token_estimate_method":"UTF8 bytes / 3 heuristic; not measured tokens","next_page":7,"next_command":"$env:PYTHONUTF8='1'; $env:PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1'; $LASTEXITCODE=$null; & 'E:/Work/keepsail/.venv/Scripts/keepsail.EXE' '--workspace' 'E:/Work/keepsail' '--json' 'change' 'context' '2026-10-27-harness-knowledge-context' '--entry' 'ev_01M61RB2S36P4YXNEBAC532HCF' '--page' '7'; $keepsailContextExit=$LASTEXITCODE; if($null -eq $keepsailContextExit){$keepsailContextExit=1}; [Console]::Out.WriteLine('__KEEPSAIL_CONTEXT_EXIT_V1__:ev_01M61RB2S36P4YXNEBAC532HCF:7:' + $keepsailContextExit); exit $keepsailContextExit"},"errors":[]}
